components.label: What they call the planning step
What they call the working step
A person approves or edits first
How it keeps going until it passes
Names reuse, risks or breaking changes
Reviews new PRs on its own
Limits on review or fix rounds

plan-name.name: Ask Devin
plan-name.summary: The docs page says to use Ask Devin to ask questions about your codebase, plan tasks, and generate high-context sessions. The page does not mention the !plan playbook.

execute-name.name: Devin session
execute-name.summary: The docs tell people to start one Devin session for each verifiable sub-task, so the session is the unit in which Devin works a task.

plan-hitl.omitted: Pages checked: Ask Devin, Linear, Jira, Using Playbooks, gallery bulk-plan-backlog and prd-to-tickets (docs.devin.ai). They describe a person working with Devin in conversation or Devin posting plan comments with open questions, but none states whether a person must approve or edit the plan before work starts.

plan-persist.name: PRD to tickets
plan-persist.summary: In the gallery example Devin reads a PRD and creates Linear tickets, so the plan lives in the tracker. The bulk-plan example instead posts the plan as a comment on each ticket. Ask Devin produces a prompt that starts a session; the page does not say it is saved.
plan-persist.short: Yes: Linear tickets and ticket comments

plan-contents.name: PRD to tickets
plan-contents.summary: The page's example output is tickets with an ID, title, T-shirt size, dependencies on other tickets, description, acceptance criteria and likely file paths; it is an example, not a guaranteed format. The Ask Devin page does not say its breakdown carries criteria or dependencies.
plan-contents.short: Mixed: example tickets carry both; Ask Devin unstated

verify-judge.name: unknown
verify-judge.summary: Devin runs existing tests, lint and type checks in its own environment before submitting a PR. Which checks run is set by the prompt, playbook or repo skill, not by a fixed pipeline.

verify-runs-app.name: Testing mode
verify-runs-app.summary: After a PR is created Devin can enter a testing mode: it writes a test plan for the main end-to-end flow, then once CI is green records a video of itself running the plan in the browser. The page calls the recording a quick sanity check.

verify-keeps-going.name: Auto-Fix
verify-keeps-going.summary: Devin iterates in its own environment until tests pass before submitting a PR, and the page says Auto-Fix lets it respond to review comments and CI failures until the PR is merge-ready. The in-session loop is set up by the prompt; no retry cap is documented.

loop-starts-next.name: Automations
loop-starts-next.summary: An automation fires on a trigger (schedule, ticket, GitHub, Slack or webhook) and starts a session with a saved prompt. A finished session choosing the next ticket by itself is not documented.
loop-starts-next.short: A schedule + An event or label (Automations)

loop-includes-plan.omitted: Pages checked: Automations, Linear, Jira, Using Playbooks, gallery bulk-plan-backlog and prd-to-tickets (docs.devin.ai). None states whether a plan step runs inside the automation loop, or whether a person approves one first.

design-reads.name: CLI Plan mode
design-reads.summary: Devin CLI's Plan mode profile has only read-only tools (grep, glob, read, todo, question, exit-plan), so it can look at the code but not change it.

design-form.name: CLI Plan mode
design-form.summary: The plan is written to a file that always opens with a heading and a summary paragraph; nothing beyond those is documented.
design-form.short: Plan file; heading and summary only

design-reuse.omitted: Pages checked: Commands & Flags, Essential Commands, Changelog (Stable) (docs.devin.ai). They do not say the CLI plan names reused code, risks or breaking changes; only a 'megaplan' keyword that makes it ask a clarifying question.

design-approval.name: CLI Plan mode
design-approval.summary: Leaving Plan mode shows an approval prompt with three choices: implement and accept edits, implement and bypass permissions, or plan needs changes.
design-approval.short: Approval prompt on leaving Plan mode

design-tasks.omitted: Pages checked: Commands & Flags, Essential Commands, Changelog (Stable), Subagents (docs.devin.ai). The plan profile has a todo tool, but no page says the plan is split into tasks or stored beyond the plan file.

plan-clarify.name: Question tool
plan-clarify.summary: The plan profile carries a question tool, and a changelog entry says a keyword such as megaplan makes the agent plan more widely and always ask at least one clarifying question before writing.
plan-clarify.short: Question tool; megaplan always asks one

plan-assumptions.omitted: Pages checked: Commands, Essential, Changelog (docs.devin.ai, Devin CLI Plan mode). No assumptions or open-questions output is described. Not documented.

plan-editable.name: No, plan needs changes
plan-editable.summary: The exit prompt offers "No, plan needs changes", which sends the plan back for revision. Editing the plan file directly before approving is not documented.

plan-saved.name: Plan file
plan-saved.summary: The plan is written to a file that always has a heading and a summary paragraph. The path is not documented.

plan-ordering.omitted: Pages checked: Commands, Essential, Changelog (docs.devin.ai, Devin CLI Plan mode), Subagents. Not documented.

plan-parallel.omitted: Pages checked: Commands, Subagents (docs.devin.ai). The plan profile's tool list has no subagent tool and the subagents page says nothing about plan mode. Not documented.

plan-replan.omitted: Pages checked: Commands, Essential, Changelog (docs.devin.ai, Devin CLI Plan mode). The mode can be switched back with /plan, but no page describes that as a re-plan step. Not documented.

plan-critique.omitted: Pages checked: Commands, Changelog, Subagents (docs.devin.ai). A custom reviewer profile for code changes is shown, not a plan critique. Not documented.

plan-readonly.name: Plan profile
plan-readonly.summary: The plan profile is defined by a list of read-only tools (grep, glob, read, todo, question, exit-plan); later entries add read-only web fetch, web search and read-only MCP tools.

plan-tracker.omitted: Pages checked: Commands, Essential, Changelog (docs.devin.ai, Devin CLI Plan mode). Not documented.

plan-human-only.omitted: Pages checked: Commands, Essential, Changelog (docs.devin.ai, Devin CLI Plan mode). Not documented.

plan-rollout.omitted: Pages checked: Commands, Essential, Changelog (docs.devin.ai, Devin CLI Plan mode). Not documented.

verify-checks.name: Self-check before PR
verify-checks.summary: In a cloud session Devin runs existing test suites, linting and type checks before it opens the PR, and iterates until the tests pass. Which checks run is set by the prompt, playbook, AGENTS.md or a skill.
verify-checks.short: Tests, lint, type checks before the PR

verify-criteria.name: Playbook Specifications
verify-criteria.summary: No product step turns criteria into checks. The guide tells the person to state success in measurable terms, and a playbook's Specifications section lists what must be true when the work is done.
verify-criteria.short: Prompt advice; playbook lists end state

verify-test-plan.name: Testing mode
verify-test-plan.summary: Testing mode, run after the PR, picks the most important flow and sends a concrete step plan before running it. The plain cloud session plans tests only as the prompt asks.
verify-test-plan.short: Testing mode writes a plan; sessions do not

verify-ci-gate.name: Branch protections
verify-ci-gate.summary: Devin is bound by the same branch protections and policies as a human engineer. The page names no specific required checks.
verify-ci-gate.short: Bound by the repo's branch protections

verify-limits.name: Playbook coverage target
verify-limits.summary: Coverage targets appear only as playbook and AGENTS.md examples (90% or 80%) that a team copies; nothing in the product enforces them.
verify-limits.short: Coverage targets are examples, not enforced

verify-test-guard.name: Playbook Forbidden Actions
verify-test-guard.summary: The gallery test playbook forbids changing source modules to ease testing, but does not forbid deleting or loosening existing tests. No built-in guard is documented.
verify-test-guard.short: Playbook example forbids editing source only

verify-evidence.name: Session Tools
verify-evidence.summary: Browser screenshots and videos can be sent back as proof of testing, and a Progress tab shows command history and output. Testing mode attaches a processed recording.

verify-pr-fix.name: Auto-Fix
verify-pr-fix.summary: Devin pushes new commits for CI failures and review feedback on PRs its sessions work on; Auto-Fix lets it iterate without being asked.
verify-pr-fix.short: Pushes commits for CI and review

route-trigger.name: Devin Review
route-trigger.summary: Auto-review starts when a PR is created (drafts included) or marked ready, or when someone with write access comments /devin review.
route-trigger.short: On PR created or ready, or /devin review

route-rereview.name: Devin Review cadence
route-rereview.summary: Cadence is a setting: Only once, or Every push; otherwise a person re-runs the review from the PR actions menu.
route-rereview.short: Setting: only once or every push

route-approve.name: Autoapprover
route-approve.summary: Devin Review does not approve or request changes; people do. A beta Autoapprover can approve the reviewed commit, and whether the repo counts that toward merge is not documented.
route-approve.short: Beta Autoapprover only; reviewer does not

route-fix-comments.name: Devin Review auto-fix
route-fix-comments.summary: On a PR a Devin session owns, findings go to the session first and only unfixed ones post as comments; on other PRs Auto-fix starts a new session.
route-fix-comments.short: Session fixes findings on its own PRs

route-fix-ci.name: Auto-Fix
route-fix-ci.summary: With Auto-Fix on, Devin iterates on failing CI checks on PRs its sessions work on.

route-fix-conflicts.name: Stacked PRs
route-fix-conflicts.summary: Conflicts are resolved quietly for stacked PRs. For a single PR, conflict repair is not documented on the Devin Review or Auto-Fix pages.
route-fix-conflicts.short: Stacks only; single PR not documented

route-limits.name: Per-PR spend limit
route-limits.summary: One cost cap per PR for auto-review (ACUs or dollars); once hit, auto-review stops for that PR. A cap on fix rounds is not documented.
route-limits.short: Per-PR spend cap, no round cap

route-state.name: Devin Review
route-state.summary: State sits on GitHub (optional commit status, PR comments) and in Devin (review history in the webapp, the owning session).
route-state.short: GitHub comments plus webapp review history

verify-hidden-tests.omitted: Pages checked: SDLC integration, Instructing Devin Effectively, Best Practices, Code Coverage tutorial, Testing & Refactoring prompts (docs.devin.ai); every page has the same session write and run its own tests. Not documented; checked on 2026-10-29.

verify-test-quality.name: Code coverage
verify-test-quality.summary: Only coverage and assertion style. The Code Coverage tutorial measures the share of functions covered; no page documents a check that the new tests would catch a bug.
verify-test-quality.short: Coverage only; nothing checks test strength

demoable.summary: The Free self-serve plan lists limited Devin usage, plus access to Devin Review and DeepWiki.

plan-name.name: Spec Mode
plan-name.summary: The Interaction Modes page offers Spec Mode, which plans before implementation: Droid investigates and proposes a plan before any code changes. Missions, a separate mode, coordinate larger multi-feature work with an orchestrator.

execute-name.name: Worker session
execute-name.summary: In a Mission, each feature gets a fresh worker session with clean context, and the page uses 'workers' for the same thing.

plan-hitl.name: Specification Mode
plan-hitl.summary: Droid researches read-only and proposes a plan; nothing is edited until the person approves, and the person can approve or keep iterating on it. In Missions, execution starts once the plan is approved.

plan-persist.name: Specification Mode
plan-persist.summary: Once approved, the plan can optionally be saved as a dated Markdown file (default .factory/docs). Whether Spec Mode splits it into separate tasks is not documented.
plan-persist.short: Yes: Spec Mode can save a file

plan-contents.name: Missions plan
plan-contents.summary: A Mission plan is features grouped into milestones, and each feature has its own validation criteria visible in the Factory App. Explicit dependency edges between features are not documented (ordering is mentioned).
plan-contents.short: Mixed: Missions criteria; dependencies not documented

verify-judge.name: Validation workers
verify-judge.summary: Validation workers run at the end of each milestone, verifying its work, and Missions validate their own work by exercising the running application.

verify-runs-app.name: User-testing validation
verify-runs-app.summary: Missions validate their own work by exercising the running application; each feature is checked by user-facing QA against the running app, which needs a script that can start or mock the app.
verify-runs-app.short: Yes, QA against the running app

verify-keeps-going.name: Stop hook
verify-keeps-going.summary: A user-written hook runs when Droid is about to finish; a block decision with a reason keeps it working, so a script can require a check before it stops. Not a built-in loop: plain sessions and droid exec are not documented as retrying.

loop-starts-next.name: Mission orchestrator
loop-starts-next.summary: After each feature or milestone finishes, the orchestrator starts the next work from the plan. Separately, scheduled automations (for example the "Ticket to PR" starter, every 15 minutes) pick up ready tickets.
loop-starts-next.short: A finished run + A schedule (Missions, automations)

loop-includes-plan.name: Missions plan approval
loop-includes-plan.summary: A Mission's plan is built with the person and must be approved before execution starts; the docs describe the orchestrator working from that plan and do not describe it re-planning during execution.
loop-includes-plan.short: No: plan approved before it runs

design-reads.name: Spec Mode
design-reads.summary: Spec Mode is read-only: Droid searches the repo, reads files, inspects linked artifacts and asks questions, and changes nothing until the plan is approved.

design-form.name: Spec Mode
design-form.summary: A concrete implementation plan is shown for review; it can optionally be saved as a Markdown file once a setting is on. No fixed template is shown.

design-reuse.name: Spec Mode
design-reuse.summary: Reuse comes only if the person asks: the docs advise naming existing patterns in the request, but no page says the plan must list reuse, risks or breaking changes.

design-approval.name: Spec Mode
design-approval.summary: When the plan is ready Droid calls an exit-spec-mode tool to ask for approval; the person then proceeds or keeps iterating.

design-tasks.omitted: Pages checked: Interaction Modes, Droid CLI Quickstart, Droid CLI Reference, Custom droids (docs.factory.com). After approval the same session implements the plan; no page says it is split into stored tasks.

plan-clarify.name: Spec Mode
plan-clarify.summary: Droid may ask clarifying questions while it researches, and the person can keep iterating before approving. There is no separate interview step that questions the person first.

plan-assumptions.omitted: Pages checked: Interaction Modes, Droid CLI Quickstart, Droid CLI Reference, Droid Exec, Custom droids (docs.factory.com, Spec Mode). The docs only advise the person to state constraints and how to verify in the request. Not documented.

plan-editable.name: Spec Mode
plan-editable.summary: The person can reject the plan and keep iterating in Spec Mode. Editing the proposed plan text directly before approving is not documented.

plan-saved.name: Save spec as Markdown
plan-saved.summary: Optional: with the setting on, an approved plan is written as a dated Markdown file (default folder .factory/docs). With it off, the page describes the plan only in the session.
plan-saved.short: Optional Markdown file, off by default

plan-ordering.omitted: Pages checked: Interaction Modes, Droid CLI Quickstart, Droid CLI Reference, Droid Exec, Custom droids (docs.factory.com, Spec Mode). The page says only that the plan is concrete and shows no step graph. Not documented.

plan-parallel.omitted: Pages checked: Interaction Modes, Droid CLI Quickstart, Custom droids (docs.factory.com). Subagents can run in parallel, but the page does not say the plan is split that way. Not documented.

plan-replan.omitted: Pages checked: Interaction Modes, Droid CLI Quickstart, Droid CLI Reference, Droid Exec, Custom droids (docs.factory.com, Spec Mode). Shift+Tab switches modes both ways, but no page describes that as a re-plan step. Not documented.

plan-critique.omitted: Pages checked: Interaction Modes, Droid Exec, Droid CLI Reference (docs.factory.com). A different model can be chosen for the planning phase, which is a model choice and not a second model reviewing the plan. Not documented.

plan-readonly.omitted: Pages checked: Interaction Modes, Custom droids, Droid Exec (docs.factory.com). For the interactive main session the page says what Droid should not do and names no tool list, so no label is given; only subagents have a stated restriction. Not documented.

plan-tracker.omitted: Pages checked: Interaction Modes, Droid CLI Quickstart, Droid CLI Reference, Droid Exec, Custom droids (docs.factory.com, Spec Mode). The plan is shown in the session and optionally saved as a file. Not documented.

plan-human-only.omitted: Pages checked: Interaction Modes, Droid CLI Quickstart, Droid CLI Reference, Droid Exec, Custom droids (docs.factory.com, Spec Mode). Not documented.

plan-rollout.omitted: Pages checked: Interaction Modes, Droid CLI Quickstart, Droid CLI Reference, Droid Exec, Custom droids (docs.factory.com, Spec Mode). Not documented.

verify-checks.name: Validation workers
verify-checks.summary: Validation workers run at the end of each milestone, exercising the running application. Which exact commands run is not named; it follows the project.

verify-criteria.name: Validation criteria
verify-criteria.summary: Each feature carries validation criteria, visible with its commits in the Factory App. How they map to test files is not documented.

verify-test-plan.name: Mission planning
verify-test-plan.summary: Planning sets milestones, which set how often validation runs. Per-feature test lists are not documented.
verify-test-plan.short: Milestones set validation cadence; no test lists

verify-ci-gate.omitted: Pages checked: Missions overview, planning, reference, running-cli, running-app, Software Factory overview, Droid Exec overview (docs.factory.com). Not documented for Missions.

verify-limits.name: Mission cost floor
verify-limits.summary: The cost floor is about one run per feature plus two per milestone, and validation can be turned off in Mission Control settings. No coverage limit is documented.
verify-limits.short: Cost floor and a validation off switch

verify-test-guard.omitted: Pages checked: Missions overview, planning, reference, running-cli, running-app, factory.com/news/missions. Not documented; the news post only says each feature gets a fresh worker session, which is not a test guard.

verify-evidence.name: Mission Control
verify-evidence.summary: Mission Control lists every worker and milestone in a live progress log, shows each worker's terminal output and reasoning, and opens a feature's validation criteria and commits. Screenshots from Mission QA are not documented.

verify-pr-fix.omitted: Pages checked: Missions overview, planning, reference, running-cli, running-app (docs.factory.com). Post-PR fixes are not documented for Missions.

route-trigger.name: Droid Review
route-trigger.summary: The review workflow runs on PR opened, pushed, reopened or marked ready (drafts skipped), or on an @droid comment; automatic_review defaults to false, so automatic is opt-in.

route-rereview.name: Droid Review
route-rereview.summary: The workflow fires again on each push, so a push starts a review where automatic review is on. How old comments are deduplicated is not documented.
route-rereview.short: Each push, if automatic review is on

route-approve.name: Droid Review
route-approve.summary: The reviewer submits an approval when it finds no issues. Whether that satisfies branch protection is not documented.
route-approve.short: Approves when it finds no issues

route-fix-comments.name: Review Comment Fixer
route-fix-comments.summary: A Custom Automations starter makes the change a teammate asks for in a PR comment, pushes one commit and replies. Droid Review itself is not documented as fixing.
route-fix-comments.short: Starter automation pushes one fix commit

route-fix-ci.omitted: not documented; checked Automated Code Review, Custom Automations (a checks-completed trigger exists, no CI-fix starter), Delegations

route-fix-conflicts.omitted: not documented; checked Automated Code Review, Custom Automations, Delegations

route-limits.omitted: not documented; a review-round cap is not on Automated Code Review or Delegations (only platform rate limits on automations)

route-state.name: Droid Review
route-state.summary: The workflow needs a token with write access to pull requests, contents and issues, so comments land on the PR in GitHub. Other state is not documented.
route-state.short: Comments on the PR in GitHub

verify-hidden-tests.omitted: Pages checked: missions overview, planning, reference, running-app, factory.com/news/missions. Validators are a different worker from the builder, but whether criteria are kept from the builder is not stated. Not documented; checked on 2026-10-29.

verify-test-quality.omitted: Pages checked: missions overview, planning, reference, running-app, factory.com/news/missions. Validators run tests and look for regressions; nothing measures the tests. Not documented; checked on 2026-10-29.

plan-name.omitted: Pages checked: Research, plan and iterate; About Copilot cloud agent; the 2026-04-01 changelog post (docs.github.com, github.blog). They describe asking for a plan before changes, but none names the planning feature; 'Research, plan and iterate' is a how-to page title.

execute-name.name: Copilot cloud agent
execute-name.summary: The docs say Copilot cloud agent can research a repository, plan changes, and implement them in the background.

plan-hitl.name: Research, plan and iterate
plan-hitl.summary: The cloud agent shows a plan before making changes; the person reviews it and iterates with follow-up prompts until it matches their intent, then asks it to implement. In Copilot CLI plan mode the person chooses to accept the plan before autopilot starts.
plan-hitl.short: Yes: review and iterate on the plan

plan-persist.omitted: Pages checked (docs.github.com): Research, plan and iterate; Copilot CLI autopilot; Copilot on GitHub.com; Best practices; Dynamic workflows. They say the plan is shown in the conversation or executed by the same session; none says it is saved as a file or tracker items.

plan-contents.omitted: Pages checked (docs.github.com): Research, plan and iterate; Copilot CLI autopilot; Best practices; improve-a-project tutorial. None says a plan is split into tasks carrying acceptance criteria or dependencies (the tutorial has the person check criteria on issues Copilot creates from findings, which is not plan output).

verify-judge.name: Cloud agent session
verify-judge.summary: The agent works in its own GitHub Actions environment, where it runs tests and linters to validate changes. How the results decide whether it keeps going before opening the PR is not documented.

verify-runs-app.omitted: Pages checked: Managing agent sessions, Using cloud agent on GitHub, Best practices for the cloud agent (docs.github.com). They say the agent runs tests and linters and can build and validate in its environment, but none says it starts the app or drives it as a user.

verify-keeps-going.name: agentStop hook
verify-keeps-going.summary: An agentStop hook fires when the agent finishes; its output can set decision block with a reason, which forces another agent turn. A built-in rule that the cloud agent keeps retrying until a check passes is not documented.

loop-starts-next.name: Copilot automations
loop-starts-next.summary: A saved task runs when a trigger fires: a recurring schedule, an issue created, a pull request opened, or a pull request synchronized. Picking the next ready issue by itself is not documented for automations.
loop-starts-next.short: A schedule + An event or label (automations)

loop-includes-plan.omitted: Pages checked: About automations, Creating automations, Managing rationale and approvals, Using cloud agent on GitHub (docs.github.com). None states whether a plan step runs inside the automation loop or is approved before it.

design-reads.name: Plan mode
design-reads.summary: The plan agent researches the task with read-only tools and codebase analysis to find requirements and constraints, and makes no code change until the plan is approved.

design-form.name: Plan mode
design-form.summary: A plan draft in a standard format shown in the chat: summary, breakdown of steps and open questions. It can be opened as a Markdown file.
design-form.short: Chat plan; can open as Markdown

design-reuse.name: Plan mode
design-reuse.summary: Constraints are named during research and ambiguity becomes open questions; reuse and breaking changes are not documented.

design-approval.name: Plan mode
design-approval.summary: Nothing changes until the person reviews and approves the plan, then clicks Start Implementation.

design-tasks.name: Plan mode
design-tasks.summary: The plan's steps are the units of work and there is no separate task store; Start Implementation hands the plan to an agent session.

plan-clarify.name: Open questions
plan-clarify.summary: There is no question round before the draft; the questions arrive with it. The plan includes open questions on anything ambiguous, and the person can iterate to clarify requirements.

plan-assumptions.name: Open questions
plan-assumptions.summary: Open questions are part of the standard plan. Assumptions as a named part are not documented.
plan-assumptions.short: Open questions yes; assumptions not documented

plan-editable.name: Open in Editor
plan-editable.summary: The person iterates on the draft by conversation before approving. Open in Editor shows the plan as Markdown in an editor tab; whether edited text is read back by the agent is not documented.
plan-editable.short: Iterate in chat; Open in Editor

plan-saved.name: Open in Editor
plan-saved.summary: The plan lives in the chat view by default. Open in Editor produces a Markdown document in an editor tab that the person can save as a file; the page names no folder or file name.
plan-saved.short: Chat; Open in Editor gives Markdown

plan-ordering.omitted: Pages checked: Using plan mode in your IDE; Using agent mode in your IDE (docs.github.com, Plan mode in the IDE). The plan is a breakdown into actionable steps with no mention of dependencies. Not documented.

plan-parallel.omitted: Pages checked: Using plan mode in your IDE; Using agent mode in your IDE; Using subagents in your IDE (docs.github.com). The subagents page does not say the plan is split that way. Not documented.

plan-replan.omitted: Pages checked: Using plan mode in your IDE; Using agent mode in your IDE; Using subagents in your IDE (docs.github.com). The plan page describes iteration before approval only. Not documented.

plan-critique.omitted: Pages checked: Using plan mode in your IDE; Using agent mode in your IDE; Using subagents in your IDE (docs.github.com). Subagents use the same model as the main session. Not documented.

plan-readonly.name: Plan agent
plan-readonly.summary: As the page states it, the plan agent researches with read-only tools and makes no code change until the plan is approved. The page does not list the tools.

plan-tracker.omitted: Pages checked: Using plan mode in your IDE; Using agent mode in your IDE (docs.github.com, Plan mode in the IDE). The outputs named are the chat plan and the Markdown document. Not documented.

plan-human-only.omitted: Pages checked: Using plan mode in your IDE; Using agent mode in your IDE (docs.github.com, Plan mode in the IDE). Not documented.

plan-rollout.omitted: Pages checked: Using plan mode in your IDE; Using agent mode in your IDE (docs.github.com, Plan mode in the IDE). The standard plan is summary, steps and open questions. Not documented.

verify-checks.name: Cloud agent session
verify-checks.summary: The agent works in its own Actions-powered environment, where it can run automated tests and linters before it pushes. Which commands run comes from the repo's custom instructions.
verify-checks.short: Runs tests and linters before pushing

verify-criteria.name: Task acceptance criteria
verify-criteria.summary: A well-scoped task carries acceptance criteria Copilot can use to verify its work. No conversion into test files is described.
verify-criteria.short: Criteria go in the task text

verify-test-plan.omitted: Pages checked: get-the-best-results, research-plan-iterate (docs.github.com). A product-made per-task test plan is not documented; testing expectations go in the task and repository instructions.

verify-ci-gate.name: Rulesets and approval
verify-ci-gate.summary: Workflows do not run on Copilot's pushes until a person approves them, and the agent is blocked from default branches and subject to rulesets like a human.

verify-limits.name: Session limit
verify-limits.summary: A session is capped at 59 minutes, which cannot be extended. Coverage thresholds are not documented.

verify-test-guard.omitted: Pages checked: get-the-best-results, review-copilot-output, use-cloud-agent-on-github, copilot-on-github, build-guardrails (docs.github.com). Not documented; weakened tests are left to the person's review.

verify-evidence.name: Session log
verify-evidence.summary: The person sees the session log of reasoning and tools used, commit messages linking back to it, and the PR diff. Screenshots or recordings are not documented.

verify-pr-fix.name: PR follow-up
verify-pr-fix.summary: Three documented paths, each started by a person: an @copilot comment, Fix with Copilot on review comments, and a button on a failing Actions job.
verify-pr-fix.short: Fixes only when a person asks

route-trigger.name: Copilot code review
route-trigger.summary: By default Copilot reviews only when someone requests it as reviewer. Automatic reviews (PR opened, or draft marked ready) are a setting per user, repository or organization.
route-trigger.short: Automatic is a setting, off by default

route-rereview.name: Review new pushes
route-rereview.summary: Copilot reviews a PR once unless Review new pushes is on; a person can re-request a review.
route-rereview.short: Once, unless Review new pushes is on

route-approve.name: Copilot approvals
route-approve.summary: The default is a Comment review that counts for nothing. With approvals on (public preview, off by default) Copilot can approve like a teammate, and a later push dismisses it.

route-fix-comments.name: Fix with Copilot
route-fix-comments.summary: When asked (Fix with Copilot, or an @copilot mention), the cloud agent implements review comments as commits or a new PR. Starting on its own is not documented.

route-fix-ci.name: Fix with Copilot
route-fix-ci.summary: When asked from a failing Actions run page, the cloud agent investigates and pushes a fix. A person must approve workflow runs on its push. Starting without a person is not documented.
route-fix-ci.short: Cloud agent fixes CI when asked

route-fix-conflicts.name: Fix with Copilot
route-fix-conflicts.summary: When asked (Fix with Copilot in the merge box, or @copilot), the cloud agent resolves the conflict, checks build, tests and linter, then asks the person for review.

route-limits.name: Code review budget
route-limits.summary: A round cap per PR is not documented. Reviews are billed per review and stop when the applicable budget is used up; a cloud agent session runs at most 59 minutes.
route-limits.short: Budget limits only, no round cap

route-state.name: Copilot code review
route-state.summary: State sits on the PR: review comments, an overview comment with the approval assessment, and the approval itself as a PR review.
route-state.short: Review comments and overview on the PR

verify-hidden-tests.omitted: Pages checked: get-the-best-results, improve-a-project, configuring-agent-settings (docs.github.com). The agent runs the repo's own tests, so nothing says any check is withheld. Not documented; checked on 2026-10-29.

verify-test-quality.omitted: Pages checked: get-the-best-results, improve-a-project (docs.github.com). Code Quality coverage thresholds exist on another surface; coverage, not strength. Not documented; checked on 2026-10-29.

plan-name.name: GitHub Issue Triage
plan-name.summary: The Software Factory page names the triage automation GitHub Issue Triage: it prioritizes issues, checks dependencies and establishes acceptance criteria before applying ready-for-dev.

execute-name.name: GitHub Issue to PR
execute-name.summary: The Software Factory page names the developer automation GitHub Issue to PR; it watches the ready-for-dev trigger label and opens pull requests.

plan-hitl.name: Software Factory triage
plan-hitl.summary: The triage agent runs as an automation that checks every 5 minutes: it prioritizes issues, checks dependencies, establishes acceptance criteria, then applies the ready-for-dev label. The page describes no step where a person approves or edits the result; the person writes the issues and acceptance criteria beforehand.

plan-persist.name: ready-for-dev label
plan-persist.summary: The output of triage is the GitHub issue carrying the ready-for-dev label, which the developer automation watches. A separate task list or plan file is not documented.

plan-contents.name: Software Factory triage
plan-contents.summary: The triage agent checks the issue's dependencies and establishes acceptance criteria before applying ready-for-dev. How the criteria are written is not documented.
plan-contents.short: Yes: triage checks dependencies and criteria

verify-judge.name: Goal Completion Loop
verify-judge.summary: In the SDK, a second judge LLM audits the transcript for evidence, such as test output, that proves the objective is complete. The Issue to PR automation lists running tests as a step but does not document what happens when they fail.

verify-runs-app.name: QA agent
verify-runs-app.summary: The QA agent (a GitHub Actions plugin, or the /qa-changes skill) runs the changed software rather than the test suite and posts a PASS, FAIL or PARTIAL report as a PR comment. It works from the PR after it is open.

verify-keeps-going.name: Goal Completion Loop
verify-keeps-going.summary: After each agent run the judge decides whether the objective is provably complete; if not, the agent is re-prompted with what is missing and runs again, up to a cap, after which the result is capped.

loop-starts-next.name: Software Factory
loop-starts-next.summary: Four automations poll every 5 minutes. GitHub labels and statuses are the queue, and the next labeled issue is taken at the next poll.

loop-includes-plan.name: Software Factory triage
loop-includes-plan.summary: The triage automation runs on the same 5-minute poll: it prioritizes issues, checks dependencies and establishes acceptance criteria before applying the ready-for-dev label, which triggers the developer automation. No person approves in between.

design-reads.name: Planning agent
design-reads.summary: In the SDK example the planning agent gets only file search, content search and an editor limited to writing PLAN.md, so it can look at the code but not change it.

design-form.name: Planning agent
design-form.summary: A file, PLAN.md, written to a fixed outline in the planning agent's system prompt: objective, context, approach with rationale, and steps.

design-reuse.name: Planning agent
design-reuse.summary: The outline asks for relevant components, constraints and the rationale for the approach; reuse of existing code and breaking changes are not documented.

design-approval.omitted: Pages checked: Creating Custom Agent, Task Tool Set, File-Based Agents, Ask Oracle (docs.openhands.dev). The example script runs the execution agent straight after planning with no pause, which is how the sample is written, not a stated policy.

design-tasks.name: Planning agent
design-tasks.summary: PLAN.md is the handoff: the second agent is told to read it and implement every component. There is no task list beyond the plan's own step list.
design-tasks.short: PLAN.md step list is the handoff

plan-clarify.omitted: Pages checked: Creating Custom Agent, Task Tool Set, File-Based Agents, Ask Oracle (docs.openhands.dev, planning agent then execution agent). The SDK example's task text tells its planning agent not to ask clarifying questions, but that is the example's prompt, not a stated property of the planning preset. Not documented.

plan-assumptions.omitted: Pages checked: Creating Custom Agent, Task Tool Set, File-Based Agents, Ask Oracle (docs.openhands.dev, planning agent then execution agent). The fixed plan outline has no assumptions or open-questions part. Not documented.

plan-editable.omitted: Pages checked: Creating Custom Agent, Task Tool Set, File-Based Agents, Ask Oracle (docs.openhands.dev, planning agent then execution agent). There is no approval point, and no page describes editing the plan between the two phases. Not documented.

plan-saved.name: PLAN.md
plan-saved.summary: A file named PLAN.md in the conversation's workspace folder. The planning agent's editor tool can write that one file only.

plan-ordering.name: Step list
plan-ordering.summary: The outline asks for step-by-step implementation steps, so order is implied by the list. Explicit dependencies between steps are not documented.

plan-parallel.omitted: Pages checked: Creating Custom Agent, Task Tool Set, File-Based Agents, Ask Oracle (docs.openhands.dev, planning agent then execution agent). The Task Tool Set page calls sub-agent delegation a fit for sequential blocking work. Not documented.

plan-replan.omitted: Pages checked: Creating Custom Agent, Task Tool Set, File-Based Agents, Ask Oracle (docs.openhands.dev, planning agent then execution agent). The sample runs planning once and execution once, with no path back to the planner. Not documented.

plan-critique.omitted: Pages checked: Creating Custom Agent, Task Tool Set, File-Based Agents, Ask Oracle (docs.openhands.dev, planning agent then execution agent). A separate optional tool asks a differently configured model for a one-off second opinion, but the planning agent's tool list does not include it. Not documented.

plan-readonly.name: Planning agent tools
plan-readonly.summary: The planning agent is given only file-pattern search, content search and an editor limited to PLAN.md, so it has no way to run commands or edit source.
plan-readonly.short: Search tools and a PLAN.md-only editor

plan-tracker.omitted: Pages checked: Creating Custom Agent, Task Tool Set, File-Based Agents, Ask Oracle (docs.openhands.dev, planning agent then execution agent). The output is the PLAN.md file. Not documented.

plan-human-only.omitted: Pages checked: Creating Custom Agent, Task Tool Set, File-Based Agents, Ask Oracle (docs.openhands.dev, planning agent then execution agent). Not documented.

plan-rollout.omitted: Pages checked: Creating Custom Agent, Task Tool Set, File-Based Agents, Ask Oracle (docs.openhands.dev, planning agent then execution agent). The outline's only verification part is a testing section. Not documented.

verify-checks.name: Goal loop
verify-checks.summary: The agent runs whatever command the objective names (the example is a pytest run); a separate judge model audits the output and runs nothing itself.

verify-criteria.name: Goal objective
verify-criteria.summary: The written objective is the check: the judge tests each run against it, and the page's pattern is an objective that names the command that must pass.
verify-criteria.short: The written objective is the check

verify-test-plan.omitted: Pages checked: Goal Completion Loop (docs.openhands.dev). Per-task test planning is not documented.

verify-ci-gate.omitted: Pages checked: Goal Completion Loop (docs.openhands.dev). CI or branch gating is not documented for the goal loop.

verify-limits.name: Goal loop cap
verify-limits.summary: A default cap of 10 rounds ends the loop as capped. No coverage or time limit is documented.
verify-limits.short: Round cap of 10; no coverage limit

verify-test-guard.omitted: Pages checked: Goal Completion Loop (docs.openhands.dev). Not documented as a rule; the judge reads real output, which covers false claims, not edited tests.

verify-evidence.name: Goal loop outcome
verify-evidence.summary: Command output, test results and file contents sit in the conversation history the judge reads, and the outcome object carries the judge's last verdict.
verify-evidence.short: Command output and the judge's verdict

verify-pr-fix.omitted: Pages checked: Goal Completion Loop (docs.openhands.dev). Post-PR fixes are not documented for the goal loop.

route-trigger.name: Automated Code Review
route-trigger.summary: Reviews start on a non-draft PR opened, a draft marked ready, the review-this label, or openhands-agent requested as reviewer.
route-trigger.short: On open, ready, label or reviewer request

route-rereview.name: Automated Code Review
route-rereview.summary: Not by default: the synchronize trigger is left out on purpose to avoid noisy re-reviews. Re-add the label, re-request the reviewer, or add synchronize to the condition.
route-rereview.short: Not by default; re-label or re-request

route-approve.name: Automated Code Review
route-approve.summary: The reviewer prompt picks APPROVE when nothing blocks, and a dedicated bot account is the identity that approves. Whether that counts toward merge rules is not documented.

route-fix-comments.omitted: not documented; checked Automated Code Review, PR Review workflow, Software Factory (does not say how comments become a revision), GitHub Integration

route-fix-ci.name: Software Factory
route-fix-ci.summary: Failed checks lead to revisions, and the watchdog will not merge without passing Actions runs. Which automation performs the revision is not documented.

route-fix-conflicts.name: Software Factory
route-fix-conflicts.summary: The watchdog updates a stale branch before merging. Conflict resolution as such is not documented.

route-limits.omitted: not documented; checked Automated Code Review, PR Review workflow, Software Factory

route-state.name: Automated Code Review
route-state.summary: Review comments land on the PR, with a Review in progress comment edited to Review complete. Other state is not documented.
route-state.short: Comments on the PR in GitHub

verify-hidden-tests.omitted: Page checked: Goal Completion Loop (docs.openhands.dev). The judge reads the same transcript the agent produced. Not documented; checked on 2026-10-29.

verify-test-quality.omitted: Page checked: Goal Completion Loop (docs.openhands.dev). Nothing grades the tests. Not documented; checked on 2026-10-29.

demoable.summary: The GitHub repository states an MIT license and says agents can be run locally, in Docker, on VMs, or anywhere an agent server backend runs.

plan-name.name: Plan Mode
plan-name.summary: The Plan Mode page says Plan Mode creates detailed implementation plans before writing any code.

execute-name.name: Cloud Agents
execute-name.summary: The Cloud Agents page describes cloud agents as running in isolated VMs with full development environments instead of on your local machine.

plan-hitl.name: Plan Mode
plan-hitl.summary: The agent writes a plan that the person reviews and edits in chat or as markdown, then clicks Build when satisfied. If it is not right, the docs advise reverting and refining the plan rather than patching a bad build with follow-ups.
plan-hitl.short: Yes: edit the plan, then Build

plan-persist.name: Plan Mode
plan-persist.summary: The plan opens as an editable virtual file saved by default in the person's home directory; Save to workspace moves it into the repo for sharing.
plan-persist.short: Yes: plan file; Save to workspace

plan-contents.omitted: Pages checked (cursor.com): Plan Mode docs and help, Agent overview, Prompting agents, Agentic coding help, Multi-agent help, Projects. None says plan steps carry acceptance criteria. Multi-agent help says Build in Parallel keeps dependent steps in order but not how dependencies are written.

verify-judge.name: CI auto-fix
verify-judge.summary: Cloud agents automatically try to fix CI failures in PRs they create, and the repository's own CI checks are the judge. A fixed pre-delivery gate that always runs is not documented.

verify-runs-app.name: Cloud Agents
verify-runs-app.summary: The cloud agent works in a cloud VM and can build, test and interact with the changed software, controlling a desktop and browser.
verify-runs-app.short: Yes, in the cloud agent VM

verify-keeps-going.name: stop hook
verify-keeps-going.summary: Cloud agents run the stop and subagentStop hooks, which the help page says let you build self-correcting loops, and automatically try to fix CI failures in PRs they create (switch off with @cursor autofix off).

loop-starts-next.name: Automations
loop-starts-next.summary: A trigger (schedule, source-control, Slack, webhook, Linear event) starts a cloud agent with a saved prompt. One run starting the next is not documented as chaining.
loop-starts-next.short: A schedule + An event or label (Automations)

loop-includes-plan.name: Projects coordinator
loop-includes-plan.summary: The Project coordinator plans the work, delegates it to agents and brings the finished work back; with subscriptions it delegates a fix each time a bug is posted. The page does not say whether each event gets a fresh plan or whether a plan needs approval.
loop-includes-plan.short: Yes: Project coordinator plans and delegates

design-reads.name: Plan Mode
design-reads.summary: The agent asks clarifying questions, then researches the codebase with file, directory and pattern search before it writes the plan.

design-form.name: Plan Mode
design-form.summary: The plan opens as a virtual file you can read and edit, and can be saved into the repo. No fixed template is given.

design-reuse.omitted: Pages checked: Plan Mode, Plan mode help, Agent overview, Prompting agents, Using Agent in CLI (cursor.com). They do not say the plan lists reused code, risks or breaking changes.

design-approval.name: Plan Mode
design-approval.summary: The person reviews and edits the plan, then clicks Build; the page frames the mode as approving the approach first.
design-approval.short: Review and edit, then click Build

design-tasks.name: Plan Mode
design-tasks.summary: One plan and one Build click; Build in Parallel runs independent steps at once and keeps dependent steps in order. No separate task records are described.
design-tasks.short: One plan; independent steps in parallel

plan-clarify.name: Clarifying questions
plan-clarify.summary: Step one of the documented flow is the agent asking clarifying questions, and the Agent tool list has an ask-questions tool that lets the agent keep working while it waits for the answer.

plan-assumptions.name: Clarifying questions
plan-assumptions.summary: Unclear requirements are named as a reason to use the mode, and the questions are the documented route for surfacing them. A plan section for assumptions or open questions is not documented.
plan-assumptions.short: Questions yes; plan section not documented

plan-editable.name: Plan file
plan-editable.summary: The plan opens as a virtual file you can read and edit, through chat or as markdown, and work starts only when you click Build.

plan-saved.name: Save to workspace
plan-saved.summary: The plan is kept in the home directory by default; Save to workspace moves it into the repo for later reference, team sharing and documentation. It is not saved in chat only.
plan-saved.short: Home folder; Save to workspace moves it

plan-ordering.name: Build in Parallel
plan-ordering.summary: From a plan, Build in Parallel keeps dependent steps in order. How a plan marks the dependency is not documented.

plan-parallel.name: Build in Parallel
plan-parallel.summary: Build in Parallel runs the plan's independent steps at once.
plan-parallel.short: Build in Parallel for independent steps

plan-replan.name: Revert and rerun
plan-replan.summary: If the build goes wrong, the docs say to revert the files, make the plan more specific and run it again. Whether a blocked build triggers this on its own is not documented.
plan-replan.short: By restart, not a plan step

plan-critique.omitted: Pages checked: Plan Mode, Plan mode help, Cursor Agent, Multi-agent help (cursor.com, Plan Mode). The plan is reviewed by the person. Not documented.

plan-readonly.omitted: Pages checked: Plan Mode, Plan mode help, Cursor Agent, Multi-agent help (cursor.com, Plan Mode). The pages say a plan is made before writing any code but do not say whether edit tools are withheld or the agent is only told not to edit, so no label is given. Not documented.

plan-tracker.omitted: Pages checked: Plan Mode, Plan mode help, Cursor Agent, Multi-agent help (cursor.com, Plan Mode). The plan is a file, not a ticket. Not documented.

plan-human-only.omitted: Pages checked: Plan Mode, Plan mode help, Cursor Agent, Multi-agent help (cursor.com, Plan Mode). Not documented.

plan-rollout.omitted: Pages checked: Plan Mode, Plan mode help, Cursor Agent, Multi-agent help (cursor.com, Plan Mode). The separate Rollouts feature writes a rollout plan when a pull request opens, which is a different artifact from this plan. Not documented.

verify-checks.name: Cloud agent
verify-checks.summary: The cloud agent can build, test and interact with the changed software in its own VM. Which checks run is its choice from the prompt, skills, agents.md and rules.
verify-checks.short: Builds and tests in its own VM

verify-criteria.omitted: Pages checked: cloud-agent, capabilities, best-practices, skills (cursor.com/docs). Not documented; the person states criteria in the prompt, a skill or a rule.

verify-test-plan.omitted: Pages checked: cloud-agent, capabilities, best-practices (cursor.com/docs). Per-task test planning is not documented.

verify-ci-gate.name: CI subscriptions
verify-ci-gate.summary: Subscriptions wait until every check on the commit completes and return one result. Whether CI is required before a PR opens is not documented.
verify-ci-gate.short: Waits for every check; required-ness unstated

verify-limits.omitted: Pages checked: cloud-agent, capabilities, best-practices (cursor.com/docs). Coverage or speed limits are not documented as limits.

verify-test-guard.omitted: Pages checked: cloud-agent, capabilities, best-practices (cursor.com/docs). Not documented as a built-in; hooks run in cloud agents and could be written to do it.

verify-evidence.name: Artifacts
verify-evidence.summary: Artifacts (screenshots, videos and log references) are attached to the PR so the person can validate without checking out the branch.
verify-evidence.short: Screenshots, videos, logs on the PR

verify-pr-fix.name: Autofix CI failures
verify-pr-fix.summary: It tries to fix CI failures on PRs it created, skipping in set cases and after 10 follow-ups; a PR comment or setting turns it off.
verify-pr-fix.short: Fixes CI failures on PRs it created

route-trigger.name: Bugbot
route-trigger.summary: Bugbot runs automatically on every PR update, or on a cursor review or bugbot run comment. Drafts are skipped unless turned on.

route-rereview.name: Bugbot
route-rereview.summary: Each push is reviewed, looking only at changes since the last review; a newer commit cancels a run in progress, and a setting limits it to one review per PR.

route-approve.name: PR Routing & Approval
route-approve.summary: Bugbot posts findings and a check, not approvals. A separate PR Routing & Approval agent can approve low-risk PRs; whether that satisfies a required reviewer is not documented.
route-approve.short: Bugbot no; routing agent approves low-risk

route-fix-comments.name: Bugbot Autofix
route-fix-comments.summary: Optional Autofix starts a cloud agent to fix the bugs Bugbot found: off, commit to a new branch, or commit to the existing branch.

route-fix-ci.name: Cloud agent CI fix
route-fix-ci.summary: Cloud agents try to fix CI failures on GitHub Actions for PRs they created, skipping after a person pushes. Teams and Enterprise plans.
route-fix-ci.short: Cloud agents fix CI on their own PRs

route-fix-conflicts.omitted: not documented; checked Bugbot, Bugbot help, PR Routing & Approval, Cloud agent capabilities, Cloud agents help, Automations

route-limits.name: Autofix attempts
route-limits.summary: Autofix on the existing branch is capped at 3 attempts per PR, and cloud agents stop after 10 CI-failure follow-ups per PR.

route-state.name: Bugbot
route-state.summary: State sits on the PR: inline comments, a Cursor Bugbot check, and a summary comment or description.
route-state.short: Comments and a check on the PR

verify-hidden-tests.name: Verifier subagent
verify-hidden-tests.summary: Partly, as isolation and not as hidden tests: a subagent starts with a clean context and gets only what the parent puts in the prompt. Nothing says the verifier holds checks the writing agent cannot see.

verify-test-quality.omitted: Pages checked: cloud-agent, capabilities, best-practices, automations, subagents (cursor.com). A Bugbot rule can require that tests exist in a diff: presence, not strength. Not documented; checked on 2026-10-29.

demoable.summary: The docs say Cloud Agents require a paid Cursor plan and are charged at API pricing for the selected model.

plan-name.name: Plan mode
plan-name.summary: The permission modes page describes plan mode: Claude researches and proposes changes without editing source, entered with Shift+Tab or a /plan prefix.

execute-name.name: Session
execute-name.summary: The docs describe each Claude Code conversation as a session, with its own context window, where Claude gathers context, acts and verifies.

plan-hitl.name: Plan mode
plan-hitl.summary: Claude writes a plan and does not edit source files until it is approved. The person can open the plan in a text editor (Ctrl+G) and edit it; approving offers three choices: continue in auto mode, continue approving each edit, or keep planning.
plan-hitl.short: Yes: edit it, approve, or keep planning

plan-persist.name: Agent teams
plan-persist.summary: In an agent team the lead creates tasks in a shared task list, stored locally under ~/.claude/tasks/{team-name}/. Agent teams are experimental and off by default.
plan-persist.short: Yes: agent teams task list on disk

plan-contents.name: Agent teams
plan-contents.summary: Tasks in the shared task list can depend on other tasks: a pending task with unresolved dependencies cannot be claimed until they are completed. Acceptance criteria on a task are not documented.
plan-contents.short: Mixed: agent teams have dependencies; criteria undocumented

verify-judge.name: /goal
verify-judge.summary: After every turn a separate small model checks the condition. The evaluator runs no commands and reads no files, so the condition must be something the transcript shows, such as a test result the agent's own check produced.

verify-runs-app.omitted: Pages checked: Best practices, Common workflows, Run Claude Code programmatically, Use Claude Code in the cloud (code.claude.com). They advise asking for evidence such as test output or a screenshot but do not document Claude Code starting the app and driving it as a built-in step. Other pages do: the `/verify` and `/run` skills, Chrome and Computer use (see landscape/verify-grid/claude-code.md).

verify-keeps-going.name: /goal
verify-keeps-going.summary: After every turn a model checks the condition; if it is not met, Claude starts another turn using the evaluator's reason as guidance. The loop ends when the condition is met, judged impossible, or cleared by the person.

loop-starts-next.name: Agent teams
loop-starts-next.summary: In an agent team, a teammate that finishes a task picks up the next unassigned, unblocked task from the shared list on its own. Experimental and off by default.

loop-includes-plan.name: Agent teams
loop-includes-plan.summary: The team lead creates the tasks in the shared task list (with dependencies) and teammates work through them. The page does not say a person approves that task list first.
loop-includes-plan.short: Yes: team lead writes the task list

design-reads.name: Plan mode
design-reads.summary: Claude reads files and runs shell commands to explore and does not edit source; edits stay blocked until a plan is approved (with a stated exception for bypass permissions in an interactive terminal).

design-form.name: Plan mode
design-form.summary: A plan written to a file and shown for review; you can open it in your editor and change it before approving. Required sections are not documented.
design-form.short: Editable plan file; no required sections

design-reuse.name: Plan mode
design-reuse.summary: Not built in: the docs' example prompt asks which files change, and guidance says to point Claude at an existing pattern, so reuse comes from what you ask for.

design-approval.name: Plan mode
design-approval.summary: When the plan is ready Claude presents it and offers to approve (auto mode or review each edit) or keep planning.
design-approval.short: Approve, review each edit, or keep planning

design-tasks.omitted: Pages checked: Permission modes, Best practices, Common workflows, Tools reference, Interactive mode (code.claude.com). Approving ends plan mode and Claude edits in the same session; no page says the plan is split into tasks.

plan-clarify.name: Question tool
plan-clarify.summary: Claude can ask multiple-choice questions with its question tool while it plans; you answer by picking an option or typing your own text.

plan-assumptions.name: Question tool
plan-assumptions.summary: The question tool is the documented route for surfacing what Claude is unsure of. A plan section for assumptions or open questions is not documented.
plan-assumptions.short: Questions yes; plan section not documented

plan-editable.name: Ctrl+G
plan-editable.summary: Ctrl+G opens the proposed plan in your editor so you can change it before Claude proceeds, and "No, keep planning" lets you tell Claude what to change.
plan-editable.short: Ctrl+G opens plan in your editor

plan-saved.name: plansDirectory
plan-saved.summary: The plan is a file, by default under the user's Claude directory in the home folder; the plansDirectory setting moves it into the project. Not chat only.

plan-ordering.omitted: Pages checked: Permission modes, Best practices, Common workflows, Tools reference (code.claude.com, Plan mode), Large codebases. The large-codebase guidance is advice to the person, not a marked ordering in the plan. Not documented.

plan-parallel.omitted: Pages checked: Permission modes, Best practices, Common workflows, Large codebases (code.claude.com). Parallel work is a separate choice: worktrees, subagents, agent teams or /batch. Not documented.

plan-replan.name: /plan
plan-replan.summary: After approval the session leaves plan mode; to plan again, cycle back with Shift+Tab or start a prompt with /plan. Whether a blocked build triggers a re-plan on its own is not documented.

plan-critique.omitted: Pages checked: Permission modes, Best practices, Common workflows, Advisor (code.claude.com). The advisor tool is a session-wide setting that Claude decides when to call, not a plan-review step. Not documented.

plan-readonly.name: Plan mode
plan-readonly.summary: Edits stay blocked until you approve, so mostly a tool restriction. The exception is an interactive terminal session with bypass permissions available, where the block is not enforced and Claude is only told to plan.
plan-readonly.short: Tool restriction; bypass makes it instruction

plan-tracker.omitted: Pages checked: Permission modes, Best practices, Common workflows, Tools reference (code.claude.com, Plan mode). The plan is a file. Not documented.

plan-human-only.omitted: Pages checked: Permission modes, Best practices, Common workflows, Tools reference (code.claude.com, Plan mode). Not documented.

plan-rollout.omitted: Pages checked: Permission modes, Best practices, Common workflows, Tools reference (code.claude.com, Plan mode), Large codebases. The only rollback and rollout hits are unrelated. Not documented.

verify-checks.name: Verification advice
verify-checks.summary: Claude runs whatever check the person or project instructions name. There is no built-in test, lint or typecheck step.
verify-checks.short: Nothing built in; the person names checks

verify-criteria.name: Goal condition
verify-criteria.summary: The person writes the condition in a goal: one measurable end state and a stated check. The goal page's example uses include implementing a design doc until all acceptance criteria hold. Automatic conversion of criteria into tests is not in their docs.
verify-criteria.short: The person writes the condition in a goal

verify-test-plan.summary: Plan mode is optional, and the guide says to skip it if the diff fits in one sentence. The example prompt asks for tests but no test list is produced.
verify-test-plan.short: Optional plan mode; no required test list

verify-ci-gate.omitted: Pages checked: github-actions, code-review, code-review-pull-requests (code.claude.com). verify-limits.omitted: Pages checked: best-practices, code-review, code-review-customize (code.claude.com). Coverage thresholds are not documented.

verify-test-guard.name: Verification advice
verify-test-guard.summary: Only advice: ask for the root cause and not to suppress the error, or have one session write tests and another the code. No built-in protection for test files.

verify-evidence.name: Show evidence
verify-evidence.summary: The guide says to have Claude show test output, the command and its result, or a screenshot. This is advice for the prompt; no page makes it automatic.
verify-evidence.short: Advice to show output or a screenshot

verify-pr-fix.name: Cloud session auto-fix
verify-pr-fix.summary: In the interactive session there is none. A cloud session with the GitHub App and a per-PR toggle receives CI failures and review comments and pushes a fix when one is clear.

route-trigger.name: Code Review
route-trigger.summary: An Owner sets it per repository: once when a PR opens or is ready, after every push, or manual only. A person with write access can always comment @claude review.
route-trigger.short: Per-repo: on open, every push, or manual

route-rereview.name: Code Review
route-rereview.summary: Only where pushes trigger reviews (the every-push setting, or a PR subscribed with @claude review always); later reviews focus on what changed since the last one.
route-rereview.short: Only with every-push or subscribed PRs

route-approve.name: Code Review
route-approve.summary: The page says a review never approves or blocks the PR, and its check run never concludes as a failure, so the merge decision stays with the team.

route-fix-comments.name: Cloud auto-fix
route-fix-comments.summary: The review itself is read-only and pushes nothing. On another surface, cloud session auto-fix decides per review comment whether to fix it, ask the person or skip it.

route-fix-ci.name: Cloud auto-fix
route-fix-ci.summary: While auto-fix is on for a PR, the cloud session receives failed CI check events and pushes a fix when it is clear; the review service does not fix.
route-fix-ci.short: Cloud auto-fix reacts to failed checks

route-fix-conflicts.name: Cloud auto-fix
route-fix-conflicts.summary: GitHub sends no event when the base branch moves, so auto-fix cannot react on its own; the person asks Claude to rebase. Projects threads have a Resolve conflicts button.
route-fix-conflicts.short: No event; person asks for a rebase

route-limits.name: Code Review spend limits
route-limits.summary: No cap on review rounds per PR is stated. Limits are a monthly spend limit, the organization's spend limit and the credit balance; a skipped review gets a comment naming the cause.
route-limits.short: Spend and credit limits, no round cap

route-state.name: Code Review
route-state.summary: State sits on the PR in GitHub: inline comments, the review body, and a check run named Claude Code Review.
route-state.short: Comments and a check run on the PR

verify-hidden-tests.omitted: Pages checked: best-practices, common-workflows, prompt-library (code.claude.com). Plugin evals hide cases on another surface, but they test a plugin, not code Claude wrote. Not documented; checked on 2026-10-29.

verify-test-quality.name: Coverage prompts
verify-test-quality.summary: Coverage and edge cases only as prompts: ask Claude to find untested functions and add edge-case tests, with a coverage target as the goal. No tool measures whether the new tests catch a broken change.
verify-test-quality.short: Only when the prompt asks, as coverage

destination.summary: The overview points to parallel subagents, background agents, scheduled Routines and the Agent SDK for custom orchestration.

queue.name: Issues, Projects, Cycles
queue.summary: Issues are Linear's fundamental unit of work; Projects group issues around a shared outcome, and Cycles are a team's repeating planning period.

queue.name: Work items (formerly issues)
queue.summary: Work items are the building blocks of Jira and can represent a story, bug, task or another work type.

queue.name: Issues, sub-issues, Projects
queue.summary: Issues track bugs, features and ideas; sub-issues add hierarchies between issues, and Projects is integrated with issues to plan and track a team's work.
